summary: Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012, and his students included Keith Dowman and Phakchok Rinpoche.

Taku Fukuda (born 1963) works in Buddhist studies and studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He was appointed lecturer at Doho University in 1995, and his affiliations with the Eastern Institute, Doho University, and Nagoya University were attested in 2026.

Takudo Ishikawa works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career includes serving as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and holding teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935), a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others. He taught at Kanazawa University (~1976–1999) and held professorships at Komazawa and Kinjo universities.

Tampalawela Dhammaratana (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sunethradevi Pirivena, the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung (1929–2024), a scholar of Sinology and history, earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He taught at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and chaired Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).
Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College, where he studied under Charles Willemen, Tilak Kariyawasam, Sumanasiri, and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong (1865–1898) was a thinker in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wenhui Yang (~1896–1897) as well as Wang Zhengyi.
Tanaya Afroz works in linguistics, having conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya, and served as a research scholar and fellow at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Tanero Sasakawa (1870–1949) was a scholar in Sinology, history, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and held positions at Toyo University and Meiji University (~1921–1944).

Tang Junyi (1909–1978) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at National Central University and under Shili Xiong and Jian Ouyang. He later taught at West China Union University, National Central University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1963–1974).

Tang Yijie (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He later served as a professor at Peking University (~1980–2014), taught at Stanford University (~1990–1991), and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Tania Singer (born 1969) studied at the University of Marburg, Technical University of Berlin, and Free University of Berlin. She later held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~2006–2010) and Leipzig University (~2010).

Tansen Sen works in history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later teaching at Baruch College (attested 2003).
Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and went on to found Kangien in 1801.
Tanuja Ajotikar is a scholar in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. She has held posts at Harvard University, The Sanskrit Library (attested 2024–2025), and Maharishi Vedic University.

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He was appointed professor of Buddhist doctrine at the University of Tokyo in 1879 and served as superintendent of Komazawa University in 1891.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. In 2011, he was attested as an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander Leonhard Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.
